evals.name: add-log-field-shared-package
evals.prompt: I want our shared runtime npm package to add a new field to every structured log line it emits. Which source file owns that, what must I check before changing a public import path, and how do I verify the change before opening a PR? Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: src/logging.ts owns structured logging; author source and rebuild dist/ rather than editing it; check package.json exports, tsconfig.build.json and the matching test/*.test.mjs consumer contract; install with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and run pnpm test before delivery, noting it does not prove consumers have installed or deployed the change.
assertions: Names src/logging.ts as the owner of structured logging and says to edit source and build dist/ rather than editing generated dist/ output
Says to inspect the matching test/*.test.mjs consumer contract (and package.json exports / tsconfig.build.json for the published boundary) before changing a public subpath
Runs `pnpm test` before delivery and states that it does not prove any consumer has installed or deployed the new artifact

evals.name: consumer-env-name-in-fleet-runtime
evals.prompt: In fleet-runtime, a consumer app wants its LCARS dispatch identity environment variable names and rollout policy baked into src/env.ts so every app gets them. Should I add that there? Give me a decision and the plan, don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Declines: application environment names, dispatch identity, business policy and rollout stay with consumers; src/env.ts only owns generic environment normalization, and a shared primitive is added only when useful across consumers without importing their policy.
assertions: Declines to put consumer-specific environment names, dispatch identity or rollout policy into fleet-runtime, saying they remain with the consumers
Says src/env.ts owns environment normalization and a shared primitive is added only when its contract is useful across consumers without importing their policy
Notes that for an integration change the consuming import and the additional proof needed there must be identified, since the package's own tests do not prove consumer adoption
